title: Don't Discard Your Rollouts: Reusing Teacher RL Traces for Student Distillation
topic: Data-centric AI->Data-centric AI methods and tools
claim: Standard distillation discards saved teacher RL traces and regenerates data; ours reuses them via staged, metadata-driven data selection.
layout: 2 stacked panels, left-to-right flow, tree-shaped rollouts with check/cross marks
description: Two stacked rounded panels. The top panel, 'Teacher RL', shows a row of teacher checkpoints as circles (π_T^Base, π_T^(1), π_T^(n), π_T^RL), linked by arrows with ellipses. Under each circle, a fan of curved branches represents sampled completions y_i. Each branch ends in a ✓ or ✗ with a 0/1 reward beneath it. A bracket labelled D_rollouts leads by a dashed arrow to a trash can marked 'Rollouts Discarded'. The final teacher's branch fan is labelled 'Regenerate + Filter', which leads to D_synthetic and SFT for the Student. A gold arrow asks 'Can We Reuse These Rollouts?'. The bottom panel, 'Rollout Distillation', runs left to right from D_rollouts prompts x1 and x2, to an SFT box on E[r](x)=1, then to a DPO box on 0<E[r](x)<1 with an easy→hard arrow, and ends at the Student. Colors are brown for early checkpoints and green for later ones, with blue and purple for the SFT and DPO boxes.
caption: Reusing teacher RL rollouts for student distillation. Top: Canonical distillation discards the rollouts saved at every teacher RL step $n$ (completions $y_i$, rewards $r_i$, log-likelihoods $\bar{\ell}_{\mathcal{T}}^{(n)}$) and pays for a separate generation pass from the teacher (\Dsynth{}). Bottom: Our method curates the saved rollouts using the pass rate $\mathbb{E}[r](x)$: we first run SFT on the all-correct prompts ($\mathbb{E}[r](x)=1$), then DPO on the mixed-success prompts ($0<\mathbb{E}[r](x)<1$), ordered from easy to hard. Within each prompt, we rank the responses by their saved teacher log-likelihood $\bar{\ell}_{\mathcal{T}}$ and use the top correct $\tilde{y}^{+}$ and incorrect $\tilde{y}^{-}$.
abstract: RL post-training methods such as PPO and GRPO are computationally expensive, with substantial resources devoted to sampling rollouts, which contain multiple completions per prompt along with their respective rewards. Canonical distillation, however, discards these traces and uses more compute to regenerate data from the final teacher. We ask if and how we can reuse the saved teacher RL rollouts to distil student models. Reusing rollouts is non-trivial: naive SFT on the rollouts underperforms canonical distillation, and naive DPO, while performant, is unstable, collapsing on weaker students. We show that treating rollout reuse as a data selection problem using metadata already recorded during GRPO substantially reduces this gap. We use prompt pass rates to order the data, using the easiest prompts for an SFT warm start prior to using mixed-success prompts for DPO. For each prompt, we use saved teacher log-likelihoods as a proxy for selecting student-compatible completions. Across mathematical reasoning and Python coding tasks, with students from multiple model families, our two-stage recipe achieves comparable average performance to canonical distillation, while incurring no additional inference cost for dataset construction.
